math-sig-figs-s1.title: Three students weigh a 50.00 g standard mass
math-sig-figs-s1.html:
Three students each weigh the same certified 50.00 g mass four times on different balances.

Four readings by each student, in grams
StudentReading 1 (g)Reading 2 (g)Reading 3 (g)Reading 4 (g)
Ana49.1249.1349.1149.12
Ben50.3149.6250.0849.95
Cai50.0149.9950.0050.00

items.q: You want to change a volume from milliliters to liters. Which conversion factor do you multiply by?
A hiking trail is 2.45 km long. How long is it in meters?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided by 1000. A meter is smaller than a kilometer, so the number of meters must be larger.

items.q: A metal block has a mass of 12.6 g and a volume of 4.65 cm³. What is its density? Include the unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you divided volume by mass. Density is mass divided by volume, in g/cm³.

items.q: Ethanol has a density of 0.789 g/mL. What is the mass of 250.0 mL of ethanol, in grams?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided by the density, which leaves mL²/g. Multiply by g/mL so that mL cancels.

items.q: Normal body temperature is 37.0 °C. What is it in kelvin?

mistakes.why: Value: you subtracted 273.15. To go from °C to K, add 273.15.

items.q: Which setup converts 3.5 hours into seconds?
Put the steps for solving a unit conversion with dimensional analysis in order.
options: Write the given quantity with its unit
Choose a factor with the given unit on the bottom
Add factors until only the wanted unit is left
Multiply the numbers and cancel the units
Check that the size of the answer makes sense

items.q: A student converts 4250 mg to kilograms and reports 4,250,000,000 kg. What went wrong?
options: The student used 100 mg per gram in place of 1000 mg per gram
Milligrams and kilograms measure different things
Both factors were upside down, so the number grew instead of shrinking
The student should have added 1000 instead of multiplying

items.q: A medicine dose is 15 mg per kilogram of body mass. How many grams does a 42 kg patient receive?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided body mass by the dose. Multiply: kg cancels against "per kg", leaving mg, then change mg to g.

items.q: Why can a temperature in kelvin not be negative?
options: Zero kelvin is absolute zero, the coldest temperature possible
The kelvin scale counts in steps that are smaller than the degrees of the Celsius scale
Scientists agreed to drop the negative half of the Celsius scale
Kelvin is used for gases, which stop existing below zero

items.q: Which of these are SI base units? Select all that apply.
Water has a density of 1.00 g/mL. A 30.0 g plastic bead takes up 25.0 mL. Will the bead float or sink in water, and why?
options: Float: its density, 0.833 g/mL, is less than that of water
Sink: its density, 1.20 g/mL, is greater than that of water
Sink: its mass, 30.0 g, is greater than 1.00 g
Float: its volume, 25.0 mL, is greater than 1.00 mL

items.q: A runner covers 5.0 km in 25 min. Which setup gives the speed in meters per second?
What is 10³ × 10⁴?
What is 10⁵ ÷ 10⁸?
What is (10⁻²)³?
What does a negative exponent mean, as in 10⁻⁴?
options: The number 10 with its digits reversed, four times

items.q: Write 10⁻³ as an ordinary decimal number.

mistakes.why: Value: 1000 is 10³. A negative exponent means divide: 10⁻³ = 1/1000.
Value: a negative exponent does not make the number negative. 10⁻³ = 1/1000 = 0.001.

items.q: What is the square root of 10⁸?
Which expression equals 1?
What is 2³ × 2⁻⁵?
Which expressions equal 10⁶? Select all that apply.
A student writes 10⁴ + 10⁴ = 10⁸. What is the error?
options: The exponent rules apply to multiplying, not adding; the sum is 20,000
The exponents should have been multiplied to give 10¹⁶
The answer should be 10⁴, because the exponents are equal
The student made no error; adding exponents is the rule here

items.q: Evaluate (10⁻⁴ × 10⁷) ÷ 10². Give the answer as an ordinary number.

mistakes.why: Value: you added the bottom exponent instead of subtracting it. Dividing by 10² subtracts 2.
Value: you subtracted 7 instead of adding it. Multiplying adds the exponents: −4 + 7 = 3.

items.q: A cube is 10⁻² m on each side. What is its volume?
Which number is written in correct scientific notation?
A fine smoke particle is 0.000000650 m across. Write it in scientific notation (type it as, for example, 6.50e-7) in meters.

mistakes.why: Value: the exponent sign is backwards. A number smaller than 1 has a negative exponent: 6.50 × 10⁻⁷.
Value: count the places again. The decimal point moves 7 places to reach 6.50.

items.q: The distance from Earth to the Sun is about 149,600,000 km. Write it in scientific notation in kilometers, keeping four digits in the coefficient.

mistakes.why: Value: a number larger than 1 has a positive exponent. The point moved left, so the exponent is +8.
Value: count the places again: 149,600,000 needs 8 moves to become 1.496.
Value: you subtracted the exponents. Multiplying adds them: 4 + (−6) = −2.
Value: you added the coefficients. In a product, multiply them: 3.0 × 2.0 = 6.0.
Value: subtracting a negative exponent adds it: 6 − (−3) = 9, not 3.

items.q: A calculation gives 52 × 10⁵. What is this in correct scientific notation?
Which list is in order from smallest to largest?
A bacterium is about 2 × 10⁻⁶ m long and a cell in your body about 2 × 10⁻⁵ m. By how many orders of magnitude do they differ?
options: They do not differ, since both coefficients are 2
One: the body cell is about 10 times longer

items.q: Which of these are equal to 0.00560? Select all that apply.
A student types 3.2 × 10^-5 into a calculator as 3.2 × 10 EE −5 and gets 3.2 × 10⁻⁴. What went wrong?
options: The calculator rounds tiny numbers up by a factor of ten
The negative sign should have been typed with the subtraction key
Scientific notation has to be typed as an ordinary decimal
The EE key already means "× 10 to the", so the extra × 10 made the answer ten times too large

items.q: A sample contains 1.5 × 10²¹ molecules, and each molecule has a mass of 3.0 × 10⁻²³ g. What is the total mass in grams?

mistakes.why: Value: you divided the number of molecules by the mass of one molecule. Total mass = number × mass of each.
Value: you subtracted the exponents. In a product they add: 21 + (−23) = −2.

items.q: How many significant figures does 0.004050 g have?
Which measurement has exactly three significant figures?
Calculate 23.45 g ÷ 12.0 mL and report the density with the correct significant figures.

mistakes.why: Value: density is mass divided by volume, not volume divided by mass.

items.q: Add 12.52 g + 3.1 g + 0.247 g and report the total with the correct precision.
Multiply 4.36 cm × 2.1 cm to find an area, with the correct significant figures.
A student measures 3 identical bolts as 2.157 g each and reports the total of the 3 bolts as 6.5 g "because 3 has one significant figure." What is wrong?
options: The total should be rounded further, to 7 g, to match the one digit in 3
Adding the three masses keeps two decimal places, so 6.47 g
Multiplying a mass by a count of objects gives the wrong unit
The 3 is an exact count, so it does not limit the answer: 6.471 g

items.q: A graduated cylinder is marked every 1 mL. Which reading shows the right number of digits?
Which student's readings are precise but not accurate?
options: Cai, because readings that agree to 0.01 g are precise

items.q: Ana's results suggest which kind of error?
options: A random error from the student reading the display inconsistently
A significant-figures error from recording too many digits
A systematic error, such as a balance that reads about 0.9 g low
No error, since the readings are so close together

items.q: What is the average of Ben's four readings, reported to the correct precision?

mistakes.why: Value: that is the sum. Divide it by the number of readings, 4.

items.q: Why does Cai's balance report readings to 0.01 g but not to 0.001 g?
options: The standard mass has four significant figures, so the balance shows four
A third decimal place would be zero for this mass, so it is left off
Balances round to two decimal places to make averaging easier
Its last digit is already estimated; a further digit would not be measured

items.q: Put the steps for a two-step calculation (an addition, then a division) in order, so that rounding errors do not build up.
options: Do the addition and note which decimal place limits it
Keep one or two extra digits in the intermediate result
Do the division with the unrounded intermediate
Round the final answer once, to the correct significant figures

items.q: What is log 1000?
What is log (1 × 10⁻⁵)?
Calculate log (3.2 × 10⁻⁴). Give the right number of decimal places.

mistakes.why: Value: you used ln (natural log) instead of log (base 10). Use the LOG key.
Value: the sign is wrong. A number smaller than 1 has a negative log.

items.q: Calculate ln (0.50). Give the right number of decimal places.

mistakes.why: Value: you used log (base 10). ln is the natural logarithm, base e; use the LN key.

items.q: Find x if log x = 2.45. Give x with the right number of significant figures.

mistakes.why: Value: you used eˣ, the antilog of ln. The antilog of log is 10ˣ.
Value: you took the log again. To undo a log, raise 10 to that power.

items.q: Find y if ln y = −0.25. Give y to two significant figures.

mistakes.why: Value: you used 10ˣ. The inverse of ln is eˣ.

items.q: Which expression equals log (A × B)?
log 2 = 0.301. What is log 200?
One quantity is 1000 times as large as another. How do their base-10 logs compare?
options: The larger one's log is 1000 times as large
The larger one's log is 1000 more
The larger one's log is 3 more

items.q: Solve ln (A/B) = −kt for A.
Which statements are true? Select all that apply.
A student needs log (4.7 × 10⁻³) but presses LN and gets −5.36. How far off is the answer, and what is the fix?
options: It is correct, since ln and log are two names for one function
It is 2.303 times too large in size; press LOG to get −2.33
It is off by 10; divide −5.36 by 10
It has the wrong sign; the answer is +5.36
